subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: Should failed overflow compaction continue to block with manual reset/new guidance, persist only a recoverable marker, or gain a stronger provider-agnostic degraded recovery path for local-provider failures like this MLX case?
rationale: Current source intentionally blocks after recovery is exhausted, while changing it affects replay safety, session continuity, local-provider behavior, and whether a new config/provider surface is acceptable.

options.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
options.body: Add a safe degraded recovery or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider failures without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

options.title: Accept marker-first observability
options.body: Treat the open marker PR as the first supported step and leave manual reset/new recovery semantics in place for now.

options.title: Add MLX request tuning
options.body: Add a narrow request parameter only after confirming the MLX server accepts a stable field that existing `extra_body` cannot express.

recommendation.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
recommendation.body: Add a safe degraded recovery or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider failures without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is centered on compaction/context recovery semantics, matching the documented Compaction and Context Engine owner area.
